newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-KOSTNER MAKES IT TWO WINS IN A ROW.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-KOSTNER MAKES IT TWO WINS IN A ROW.

text.p: Italy's Isolde Kostner, who had to share the glory in a downhill on Friday, made it two wins in a row on Saturday with victory in a women's Alpine skiing World Cup super-G.

Kostner, the super-G world champion who was the joint winner of Friday's downhill with Switzerland's Heidi Zurbriggen, clocked one minute 17.04 seconds on the Olimpia delle Tofane piste to beat Sweden's Pernilla Wiberg by a 10th of a second.

Wiberg, the super-G and overall World Cup leader after winning four times this season, in turn beat her main World Cup rival Katja Seizinger of Germany into third place by the same slim margin. Seizinger clocked 1:17.24.
The victory was the fourth of Kostner's career with three of those wins coming in Cortina d'Ampezzo. She won a downhill here last season.

It was also the 21-year-old Italian's first super-G win of the season and underscored her rapidly improving form going into the world championships in the north-western Italian resort of Sestriere next weekend.
Italians have now won four of the last five women's World Cup races.
Kostner was second in the last super-G at Bad Kleinkirchheim, Austria, earlier this month after a third place in Val'd Isere in the previous super-G.
